descriptions.shortTag: Live card counting with 7 systems, true count, and table rules.
descriptions.oneParagraph: Counting Edge is a live blackjack card-counting trainer for Android. Tap card ranks as they fall, and the app tracks your running count, true count, player edge, and bet recommendation in real time. Seven professional counting systems — from beginner-friendly Hi-Lo to advanced Wong Halves — all rule-aware and calibrated to the exact table conditions you set. One screen. No subscriptions. No ads.
descriptions.summary: An Android Jetpack Compose training app for live blackjack card-count practice. Supports 7 counting systems, rule-aware strategy guidance, and a compact one-screen workflow.

coreCounting: Live running count updated on every card tap
True count calculation (running ÷ decks remaining) for balanced systems
Estimated player edge % from current true count and table rules
Bet recommendation ramp (1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 12 units) tied to live count
shoeAndDeckTracking: Set total decks (1 / 2 / 4 / 6 / 8) with a tap
Adjust decks remaining with a precision slider (0.25 deck steps)
Live penetration %, cards drawn, cards left, total cards
Optional Ace side count for Hi-Opt II and Omega II
strategyReference: Full-screen basic strategy chart — rule-aware, updates with current true count
Colour-coded chart cells (Hit, Stand, Double, Split, Surrender) with the action letters kept; deviations marked with *
Illustrious 18 + Fab 4 indices, scaled to each system's own true count
System cheat sheet (tag values + key deviations) per system
Counting system guides with level, balance type, and usage tips
sessionTools: One-tap Undo right beside the count pad, next to the last few cards, for correcting a missed or wrong card tap
Reset returns shoe and count to starting state, with a confirmation so a stray tap can't wipe a shoe
KO / ReKO reset returns to the deck-specific Initial Running Count (IRC), not zero
Session resume — running count, shoe depth, selected system, and table rules survive app restarts (stored locally)
Built for live use — haptic tick on every card tap, screen stays awake while counting, system back closes the strategy chart
Landscape and tablet layout with the count pad and Undo on one side and the stats on the other
drillMode: Timed running-count practice from the Menu
Pick length (26 / 52 / 78 cards) and speed (Slow / Medium / Fast)
Cards are dealt from a shuffled real shoe and flash one at a time; enter the final running count when done
Scored exact / off-by-N against the active counting system

Full table rules engine — affects both strategy display and edge calculation
Strategy deviations tied to live count — not just a static chart
No subscriptions, no ads, no locked systems, no tracking — all features available on install
Open source (Apache 2.0) and installed as a direct APK — nothing is sent off your device

faq.question: Is Counting Edge free?
faq.answer: Yes, completely. The app is open source (Apache 2.0) and distributed as a direct APK download. All 7 counting systems, the full strategy chart, drill mode, and every feature are available on install — no in-app purchases, no subscription, no ads, no tracking.

faq.question: How do I install the APK?
faq.answer: Download the APK from the website or GitHub Releases, open it on your Android device, and when Android asks whether to allow install from an unknown source, say yes for your browser or file manager. The APK is signed, verifiable with the SHA-256 published alongside each release.

faq.question: Why not Google Play?
faq.answer: Direct distribution lets us ship updates immediately without review cycles, keep the app fully free with no store fees, and keep source code and build process open for anyone to audit.

faq.question: Which counting system should I start with?
faq.answer: Hi-Lo is the standard starting point. It's balanced, level 1, and the most widely documented system. You can switch to KO or ReKO if you want to skip true count conversion. Advanced systems like Hi-Opt II and Wong Halves are there when you're ready.

faq.question: What does 'true count' mean?
faq.answer: The true count is the running count divided by the estimated number of decks remaining. It normalizes the count across different shoe sizes, making your edge estimate more accurate. Unbalanced systems like KO don't require true count conversion by design.

faq.question: Is this legal to use in a casino?
faq.answer: Card counting by itself is not illegal. Using software or devices at the table violates casino rules in most jurisdictions. Counting Edge is a training tool — use it to practice, not at the table.

faq.question: What are the system levels?
faq.answer: Level 1 systems (Hi-Lo, KO, ReKO) use simple ±1 tag values and are the easiest to learn. Level 2 systems (Hi-Opt II, Omega II, Zen Count) use a wider tag range for a small accuracy gain. Level 3 (Wong Halves) uses fractional tags for maximum precision, requiring more mental effort.
